clue.text: Paddy in sensible jumper at first gets a degree of comfort

indicators.note: coming at first means standing at the front, so this piece leads the rest

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a famous jumper

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a mature person is sensible
a paddy is a fit of temper

explanation.surface: An angry Irishman in a sensible sweater finds some comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irish name and 'jumper' like a sweater, but a paddy is a tantrum and the jumper is a kangaroo, which comes first; the tantrum sits inside the sensible word.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual indoor warmth, around twenty degrees Celsius, is the temperature people find comfortable, so it is literally one degree reading.

clue.text: Former BBC newsreader who is Jeremy Vine's wife disturbed old Cheshire calf

definitions.text: Former BBC newsreader who is Jeremy Vine's wife

indicators.note: something disturbed has been thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A famous broadcaster's wife is upset by an elderly young cow from Cheshire, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: The long definition does all the work; the three words at the end are the letters to rearrange. Jeremy Vine is a British radio and television presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachel Schofield presented news on BBC television and radio and is married to the broadcaster Jeremy Vine.

clue.text: Surgical surfaces somehow obliterate pangs

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters end up in some new order

parts.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Places where surgeons work manage to wipe out the patient's pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests anaesthesia removing pain; 'obliterate pangs' is simply the letter supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients lie on these flat tables during surgery, so they are the surfaces used in theatre.

clue.text: Complete ruin of tenor and alto transcription

definitions.note: TOTAL is a verb meaning to wreck completely; the clue phrases it as a noun

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

indicators.note: a transcription writes material out afresh, here with the letters set down in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement for two voices turns out a complete disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In choral music T and A stand for tenor and alto; rearranging T with ALTO gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To total a car is to wreck it beyond repair, an informal sense of utter destruction.

clue.text: Originally massive old avian NZ resident once

indicators.note: originally points to how things began, so only the opening letters count

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Describes an enormous ancient bird that used to live in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The three initials spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a giant flightless bird native to New Zealand, hunted to extinction centuries ago.

clue.text: A wander up to historic Portuguese city

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: A tourist's stroll up to an old city in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: A and ROVE are joined, then the whole string is turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Évora is a city in the Alentejo region of Portugal, its centre a World Heritage Site with a Roman temple.

clue.text: It's a winner during matches regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps winning in tennis matches.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'matches' give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a serve the receiver cannot touch wins the point outright, so it is an outright point-winner.

clue.text: Club name on pick-up trucks for water board in northern England

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a common football club name, as in Manchester or Leeds
a utility vehicle, or ute, is a pick-up truck in Australian English

explanation.surface: A football club's name painted on company trucks for a regional water supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Club name is a word shared by many teams, and the vehicles are utilities, from the Australian word for pick-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: United Utilities is the private company supplying water and sewerage to North West England, successor to the regional water authority.

clue.text: Conclusion — of course!

parts.note: surface reading: an emphatic 'naturally' tacked onto the word for an ending; setter's reading: the end of a golf course, where the final hole is putted out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course!' reads as an exclamation of agreement, but it means belonging to a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard golf round has eighteen holes, and the last putting surface is where the round finishes.

clue.text: Make a break-through and exploit an opportunity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally make a hole through something
second meaning: in sport, fashion a chance to score

explanation.surface: Someone achieves a breakthrough and makes the most of their chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'break-through' points to the literal sense of breaking a way through.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both physically making a gap and, figuratively, engineering a chance, as a midfielder does for a striker.

clue.text: Online extra involving ten mathematical characters

indicators.note: to involve is to entangle, so the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the first two words

explanation.surface: A bonus web feature that uses ten maths symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests symbols like pi or sigma, but it means the letters of 'ten mathematical' themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A file sent along with an electronic message is an additional item delivered over the internet.

clue.text: Brown and green phonetic letter

parts.note: tan is a light brown
a green traffic light means go

explanation.surface: A letter spoken in two colours, as if describing its look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' is not a colour here but the traffic signal meaning go.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO spelling alphabet used by radio operators, T is spoken as this word.

clue.text: Takes in poor Shona wears

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the letters are knocked into a different form

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Poor Shona is fooled by what she's wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is defined twice: at the start as deceives, at the end as is dressed in, with the rearranged name between.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone on is to tease or fool them, and to have clothes on is to be wearing them.

clue.text: Attire for the Lido with roughly two GCSEs, minimum

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or crudely, so the letters come out in a rough new order

parts.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: An entry requirement for the pool: suitable clothing plus at least two school exam passes.
explanation.walkthrough: GCSEs are the exams English pupils sit at sixteen; a lido is an open-air public swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece garment worn for bathing is what a visitor to an outdoor pool would put on.

clue.text: Tree that's found on satnav on borders of Lancashire

parts.note: a satnav displays a map

indicators.note: a border is an edge, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the county

explanation.surface: A tree that shows up on a navigation screen at the edge of a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: The satnav supplies what it shows on screen, followed by the edges of Lancashire, a county in North West England.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a common deciduous hardwood, known for its lobed leaves and syrup.

clue.text: Belief for which a Native American died

parts.note: the Cree are an indigenous people of North America
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A cause for which an Indigenous man gave his life.
explanation.walkthrough: D for died is a genealogy abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a system of religious faith or principles someone holds.

clue.text: Drunk professional taking note at popular conference for body-building regime

parts.note: high means intoxicated
pro is short for professional
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
in means fashionable, popular
a diet is a formal assembly, as in the Diet of Worms

explanation.surface: A tipsy expert at a big conference shares advice on muscle-gaining meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' and 'at' simply place the pieces one after another. A diet in the old sense is a legislative assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodybuilders eat lots of meat, eggs and shakes to add muscle, a nutritional plan rich in that nutrient.

clue.text: Former girl-friend with soldier taking steps in Spanish art form

parts.note: an old flame is a former sweetheart
non-commissioned officer
dancing is taking steps

explanation.surface: An ex-girlfriend and a soldier take lessons in a Spanish style of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: An old flame is an ex, so 'former' is needed to get from girlfriend to that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the Andalusian tradition of guitar, song and stamping footwork, recognised by UNESCO as cultural heritage.

clue.text: Function at company — just a very short time

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
just a sec means wait a moment

explanation.surface: An office party that lasts only a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a social event at work, but it is a mathematical function.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry the cosecant, abbreviated this way, is the reciprocal of the sine.

clue.text: Inhuman geek regularly at The Cloud over the channel

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A heartless nerd working at a cloud computing firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Cloud' is italicised like a title, but 'over the channel' means in France, so a French word is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the Channel in France, the everyday word for a cloud in the sky is this one.

clue.text: WW1 vessel made from scale bus remains

indicators.note: something made from materials is constructed out of them, so the letters are rebuilt into a new shape

parts.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A model First World War ship assembled from the wreckage of a scale-model bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' suggests model-making; the three words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The E class was a Royal Navy type of underwater boat that served widely in the First World War.

clue.text: The sun should even things out

indicators.note: taking out the even-numbered things leaves only the odd-numbered letters

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Sunshine ought to balance things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even things out' sounds like balancing, but it means remove the even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sol is the Latin name for our star, used in astronomy and poetry.

clue.text: Hospital space available in the garden

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a free place for a patient on a ward

definitions.note: a phrase locating the answer rather than a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a patch of soil for planting flowers

explanation.surface: A hospital with room to spare, somewhere out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Hospitals count capacity in these, and a garden has flower ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Wards measure spare capacity by free places to sleep, and gardeners plant in raised or flower plots of soil.

clue.text: Dined out with Applecross refugee

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or out of place, so the letters are set in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who fled their home eats a meal out with people from a Scottish village.
explanation.walkthrough: Applecross is a remote village in the Scottish Highlands; its letters join those of 'Dined' to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A person forced from their homeland by war or persecution is officially termed this, a phrase from post-war Europe.
